claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, rollout is limited and reversible, and the remaining school-admissions limitation can be handled through explicit model-card disclosure and monitoring.
decision_criteria: A compliant certification requires admissible evidence that the material limitation is either resolved, excluded from rollout, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Small-percentage rollout, rollback capability, and monitoring are not by themselves enough when the affected segment remains exposed.
Claims must be supported by existing admissible evidence, not by a future disclosure step that has not been evidenced.
evidence_requests: Provide the final pre-launch model card or release packet showing explicit disclosure of the school admissions advising limitation and its continued inclusion in the initial cohort.
Provide approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses the school admissions advising exposure, if certification is meant to rely on acceptance rather than disclosure alone.
Provide the launch decision artifact showing whether certification is contingent on disclosure completion before rollout.
specific_concerns: The affected school admissions advising segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The reviewed evidence shows no approved risk acceptance; the draft has a blank approver line and does not address the exposed segment.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material weakness only if the use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable.
The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations before launch unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record rather than only conditionally supportable after disclosure is completed.
That the current packet is sufficient to certify without either excluding the affected use case or producing reviewed risk acceptance tied to that exposure.
